source_text: VII. Ἔχοντες οὖν τὸ παιδάριον, τῇ παρασκευῇ περὶ δείπνου ὥραν ἐξῆλθον διωγμῖται καὶ ἱππεῖς μετὰ τῶν συνήθων αὐτοῖς ὅπλων, ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν τρέχοντες. Καὶ ὀψὲ τῆς ὥρας συνελθόντες, ἐκεῖνον μὲν εὗρον ἔν τινι δωματίῳ κατακείμενον ὑπερώῳ· κἀκεῖθεν δὲ ἠδύνατο εἰς ἕτερον χωρίον ἀπελθεῖν, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἠβουλήθη, εἰπών· Τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ γενέσθω. Ἀκούσας οὖν αὐτοὺς παρόντας, καταβὰς διελέχθη αὐτοῖς, θαυμαζόντων τῶν παρόντων τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ εὐσταθές, εἰ τοσαύτη σπουδὴ ἦν τοῦ συλληφθῆναι τοιοῦτον πρεσβύτην ἄνδρα. Εὐθέως οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐκέλευσε παρατεθῆναι φαγεῖν καὶ πιεῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, ὅσον ἂν βούλωνται· ἐξητήσατο δὲ αὐτούς, ἵνα δώσωσιν αὐτῷ ὥραν πρὸς τὸ προσεύξασθαι ἀδεῶς. Τῶν δὲ ἐπιτρεψάντων, σταθεὶς προσηύξατο πλήρης ὢν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ, οὕτως ὡς ἐπὶ δύο ὥρας μὴ δύνασθαι σιγῆσαι, καὶ ἐκπλήττεσθαι τοὺς ἀκούοντας, πολλούς τε μετανοεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ἐληλυθέναι ἐπὶ τοιοῦτον θεοπρεπῆ πρεσβύτην.
orientation: Polycarp has withdrawn to a country house after betrayal, and armed men are now coming to seize him.
pass_a_gloss: Since they had the little boy with them, on the preparation day about the hour of dinner the pursuers and horsemen went out with the weapons customary to them, as men running against a robber. And having come together late in the hour, they found him lying down in a certain upper chamber. And from there he was able to go away into another place, but he did not wish it, having said: Let the will of God come to be. Therefore having heard that they were present, having gone down he talked with them, while those present were wondering at his age and his firm composure, that there was so much eagerness for such an old man to be arrested. Immediately therefore he ordered that food to eat and drink be set before them in that hour, as much as they might wish. And he requested them, in order that they might give to him an hour to pray without hindrance. And when they permitted it, having stood he prayed, being full of the grace of God, in such a way that for two hours he was unable to be silent, and those hearing were amazed, and many were regretting that they had come against such an old man befitting God.

lemmas.gloss: small boy seized as guide here

choices.why: keeps Jewish Greek day name before the great Sabbath in section 8

choices.english: as men running against a robber
choices.why: keeps simile and hostile motion, not a neutral arrest
names visible steadiness wondered at with his age
prayer time requested from captors means undisturbed, not inner courage
keeps predicate sense without hyphen compound

pass_b_english: With the boy to guide them, they set out on the preparation day about suppertime, pursuers on foot and on horseback with their usual weapons, like men rushing out to take a robber. They arrived late and found him lying down in an upstairs room. He could still have left for another place, but he would not. Polycarp says, “May God’s will be done” (Matthew 6:10).

When he heard they were there, he came down and spoke with them, while those present marveled at his age and his firm composure, that so much urgency should go into arresting such an old man. At once he ordered them to set food and drink before them at that hour, as much as they wanted, and he asked them to give him an hour to pray without hindrance. They allowed it, and he stood and prayed, full of God’s grace, so that for two hours he could not fall silent, and his hearers were amazed, and many were sorry they had come after an old man so befitting God.
